Williams, Chase
I'll admit that I really get confused by the aff Strat at the end of the debate. I am not really sure what offense they are going for? For some reason, they seem to be spending most of the summary and FF on defense against the neg's Xi power vacuum argument. Perhaps I'm missing something big brain here - and if so, I apologize - but Neg does way more to win my ballot in the final speeches with a clear and logical story about the Xi scenario - one that makes sense to me and can be easily explained.
Even if I grant Aff some mitigation to the neg scenario - that the power vacuum will take more time in timeframe weighing - I still think the neg scenario is the most logical and most probable. Given that I live on an island just off the coast of China, I don't see a world where I'm willing to risk Taiwan's existence for the potential of some ambiguous benefits from the aff, so I negate.
McDonald, Abby
on politics, aff goes for the arg that xi will just reframe the narrative, but there isn't enough warranting on this until second final, and it also doesn't answer the analysis neg gives that xi is already on the brink of losing power + the elites would immediately oust him post-aff.
on mapping, I think neg is correct that the scenario is still reliant on taiwan being attacked first. I don't get great analysis from aff as to why china would decide to strike the US first, and I think the conceded defense that china never attacks taiwan due to separatists fears is pretty damning.
the timeframe also flows neg, since neg's analysis about their internal link triggering first goes conceded, and I buy that xi would get ousted immediately. I don't really get any coherent warranting from the aff as to why china is going to lash out soon, besides "it's perceptual" - which is lowk fake.
Liu, Tony
I vote aff for Cranbrook. I think the neg has dropped that joint ventures ensures China still gets access to REMS. This seems to answer the internal to why REMS are important for Xi which is to create leverage to the US and appear strong, if China gets the REMS through different means. The only aff response that could interact with this in the final is stated as REMS are important for Xi which misses the other warrants. The aff case seems to be a comparably higher risk because their impact ev does at least partially make the claim that China would get capabilites to attack the entire pacific not just Taiwan. I can lean neg on time frame but I don't think they win a sufficient risk of the case.

Extinction weighing is pretty much conceded, so whoever gives me the first link into extinction gets my ballot. Cartels/extinction - Aff responds with non-unique, but neg defends the causal link that offshore gambling --> organized crime, so I had to buy the magnitude weighing
-your responses were effective to mitigate neg's impacts, but you need to explain more on the link level on especially black markets and the sovereignty rhetoric to prove that FTC regulations would actually outweigh the actual lost revenue

he round was decided on the Court Clog and Cyber-Security link chain, which the Negative successfully protected and accelerated.

The "Administrative Judicial Emergency": While the Pro (Emerald AG) argued that the courts are already "fried" (Thanawala evidence), the Negative successfully turned this into a reason to negate. They argued that because the courts are at a breaking point, adding a wave of sports betting litigation—which they established would happen immediately as platforms and states challenge the FTC—would be the "last straw."

The Cyber-Security / Nuclear Escalation: The Negative won a fast-paced link that delayed justice in federal courts pushes "Data Protection" and "Cyber" cases off the docket. The Politics Wash: Both teams presented competing "Politics" narratives. The Pro argued they need a win for Midterms; the Neg argued the Dems already have momentum that the plan disrupts. Because both sides had 2026 evidence, this area of the flow became a "wash," forcing the decision onto the institutional impacts (Courts/Cyber) where the Neg had a clearer, uncontested link to terminal extinction. I vote AFF to mitigate high-probability cyber harms that can directly wipe out people’s finances and destabilize basic safety.
On framework, NEG tries to re-orient the round around structural violence first and indicts util/extinction weighing as exclusionary but that argument doesn’t get them out of the AFF world for me. The AFF is explicitly telling a structural violence story too (i.e. financial ruin, poverty impacts from cyber exploitation), so even if I grant NEG’s lens, it doesn’t function as an AFF filter. Also I don't think NEG’s “we’re not doing extinction” cleanup out of the 1NR is a full fix like kicking court clog doesn’t magically erase that the initially operation was in big-scope impact framing while now claiming that kind of calculus is illegitimate.
In terms of offense access in the back half, NEG collapses hard to the black market arg and shoves their chips on microbetting/addiction/poverty. AFF cyber is conceded at the point of collapse and on my flow the 1NR doesn’t do the work to meaningfully answer or reduce that risk beyond a thin “historically we haven’t seen large attacks," which AFF answers with a threat is now framing (e.g. China Iran other actors adopting AI, etc.).
NEG’s black market offense doesn’t close the gap for me. I buy the AFF double turn thing NEG needs gambling to be normalized/increased by the plan but AFF gives a plausible deterrence story (i.e. FTC regulation signaling risk can reduce participation), which at minimum makes NEG’s link direction unstable. NEG never gives me a crisp comparison explaining why gambling SV outweighs a conceded cyber impact under either framework especially when AFF is also explicitly weighing cyber as structural violence (poverty/financial collapse). rfd:
I negate for Heritage.
On the weighing. I think the shell uplayers the K. It is just conceded that the direction of the theory debate determines whether or not the K can be successful or indeed valuable writ large. I think the neg makes a mistake conceding the ROTB and going for the alt without articulating why theory does not come first. Especially in the context of "post fiat evaluation" theory seems critical normatively.
On theory. I think its two ships passing. I am getting the interp and violation extended that if the alternative is vague, then the affirmative cannot engage with the solvency early enough and likewise has made the debate impossible for many debaters to engage with which means the K isnt solvent. It is articulated that comprehension of the literature in this way is key to engagement with the K, testing it, and thus implementing its alternative. Additionally, the implication is that this kills real world movements. The only real response to this directly is that cross solves. I kinda agree with this, I think this round is decent evidence of that, and I am not getting a great frontline to this whatsoever. I think the interp is probably heavily mitigated by this. The counter interpretation that they defend the violation plus material movements is also conceded. The neg articulates supposedly material alternatives such as green local movements in Greece which put us back on path to connecting with the natural world. I think this also does real damage to the interpretation. The idea that we could do both more generic mindset shifts along with specific material movements seems to justify and prove the alt solvency, and makes it much less vague to me. There are two standards that come along with this CI, that are benefits of the more vague alts. These are both conceded, that constraining movements turns students into footsoldiers instead of critical thinkers, and that it precludes unique perspectives that would be beneficial to the movement. These are kinda not great but pretty conceded. The issue I have is I have zero remote idea how to weigh the the standards of the CI versus the standards of the interp. They go in entirely different directions, and so I think from them alone I dont know if vague alts are good or bad for the movements. I come down on this in favor of the negative because they read defense that cross solves the concerns with the vague alts which means the benefits of not being tied down exclusively to materiality are more unique. I buy all of the defense that fairness is not an impact but the aff does not go for fairness. That said, I wanted to point out that no one should ever lose to fairness BAD. If it is unclear why, I doubt the neg would be partial to me dropping them because of something they did not say, and then may even call that unfair.. Regardless, this is irrelevant for the debate. So, I think that vague alts are probably not bad and maybe even good in the context of this debate. What this does is at the very least mean any offense on the K is offense enough to vote on because the aff goes for nothing else.
The K proper is conceded. The only issue I have is the neg cannot fiat anything in PF, but the aff goes about conceding the utopian alts thing so it seems as though I do and the aff explanation for why I can do the aff with the mindset shift after they defended their original mindset is entirely insufficient given the links. I think worst comes to worst for the neg and I think there is no offense because they cannot fiat it, I would still presume first or neg so any way I go about it I negate.

That Britain is uniquely Eurocentric now which means they will want to cooperate and that the common threat of cyber attacks brings the nations together.

Miscalc and cyber bipass MAD which makes them more probable to other nuclear war links
